in_text_mentions: idney of 12.3 cm, left kidney of 13.2 cm, with multiple bilateral renal calculi, the largest 10mm in diameter. The right renal pelvis was dilated (1.2 cm), and a simple 10 mm cyst seen in the left kidney. The bladder was normal. A CT urogram revealed a 2 mm calcification seen to the left of the true renal pelvis, suggestive of an intraluminal ureteric calculus. Intravenous pyelogram further demonstrated paintbrush-like appearances of the renal pyramids, consistent with MSK (Figure 2). The patient had the most severe form of MSK, grade 4, with involvement of all the calyces in both kidneys [8].

in_text_mentions: On examination he weighed 17.5 kg (-3SD), his height was 111 cm (-6SD), head circumference 47 cm (-3SD), weight for height was -1SD to –2SD indicating significant growth failure. Facial dysmorphism characterized by small head, large ears, broad nose, prognathism, malocclusion of teeth were noted along with prominent nipples. There was extensive acanthosis nigricans, hypertrichosis, thick finger nails and coarse hands (Figs. 1 and 2).Fig. 1Coarse facies Fig. 2Acanthosis nigricans and hypertrichosis

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal clinical photograph of a girl with genetically confirmed Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome showing coarse facial features (thick lips, wide nasal root, bulbous nasal tip, hypertelorism) as described in the caption and in-text. Article title confirms RMS diagnosis. Article describes incomplete phenotypic presentation, hence variant typicality. B: Close-up clinical photograph of the patient's ear demonstrating a large, low-set ear as described in the in-text mention ('large, low set ears (Fig. 1)'). This is a recognized feature of Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome facial dysmorphism. Specific ear finding not in vocabulary, hence proposed_findings.

The broad nose, large ears and coarse facies support coarse facial features, while irregular, crowded, dysplastic teeth support the vocabulary entry for premature eruption of dysplastic teeth. The caption also identifies a fissured tongue, although that manifestation is not included in the allowed findings vocabulary. The black eye bar is a privacy redaction annotation, not a third-party copyright mark.

findings.evidence: Caption: 'Thickened nails.' In-text: 'Examination of the nails showed thickened nails (Fig. 5).'

panels.rationale: Real clinical photograph of human hands from a case report of probable Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome. The panel shows thickened/dystrophic fingernails, directly supported by the caption 'Thickened nails' and in-text mention linking Fig. 5 to nail examination. A black annotation box highlights the affected nail.
